title: CAST antiarrhythmic trial: arrhythmia suppression did not translate into survival and increased mortality
summary: The Cardiac Arrhythmia Suppression Trial is promoted as a high-sensitivity medical reversal record. The trial tested whether suppressing asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic ventricular arrhythmias after myocardial infarction would reduce mortality. Patients whose ventricular ectopy could be suppressed were randomized to active drug or placebo; the encainide and flecainide arms were stopped because of excess mortality. This is a canonical case in which a plausible and measurable surrogate endpoint did not predict patient survival and instead masked drug harm.
